comparator.name: Bachelor Business Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: Articles 12.1–12.2 and 16.3–16.5 of the adopted Business Engineering regulations govern the September 2026 standard pathway. The EER, nominal schedule and dated catalogue support 60 EC each year. The nine 5 EC electives come from a published Business Engineering list, with approved outside substitutions governed separately. BENP2004 is recorded as 20 EC overall, comprising 2.5 EC of thesis preparation and 17.5 EC of thesis research. It includes an internship and individual paper, presentation and defence. Students must be in their third year and have completed all first-year components before starting the thesis research. Internship Office approval is required. Binding study advice uses 45 first-year EC without a named-course threshold. The standard pathway keeps the required third-year skills course and project. An approved study-abroad semester is optional.

basisLabels: Physical-science and engineering principles: mechanics, energy, materials and production processes
courseTraceability.rationale: Sustainability Essentials I teaches the physics, chemistry, materials-science, mathematics and modelling concepts needed to analyse sustainability problems and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's Fundamentals of Engineering (basic engineering principles, elementary modelling and energy); it is not a substitute for the target's mechanics, electricity, fluids and heat-transfer content, and it is the formal prerequisite for Sustainability Essentials II. It implements the explicit academic basis “Physical-science and engineering principles: mechanics, energy, materials and production processes”.

basisLabels: Economics, finance and business functions: micro- and macroeconomics, markets, and corporate finance and investment decisions
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Economics covers supply and demand, consumer theory, the theory of the firm and market structures in microeconomics and aggregate output, unemployment, inflation and goods and financial markets in macroeconomics, and directly implements the micro- and macroeconomic content of the target's Economics for Business Engineering. It implements the explicit academic basis “Economics, finance and business functions: micro- and macroeconomics, markets, and corporate finance and investment decisions”.

basisLabels: Research and development and independent research: laboratory and research skills, an R&D project with an external research question and a bachelor thesis

It implements the explicit academic basis “Research and development and independent research: laboratory and research skills, an R&D project with an external research question and a bachelor thesis” and “Product and process design and sustainability engineering: designing products and production processes under technical and business constraints, with circular-economy and life-cycle assessment projects”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first plan retains the sustainable technology and business anchor. The second retains the computational and modelling anchor, with AI adoption and governance replacing the regional sustainability project. Laboratory biology cannot supply the materials and process laboratory sequence. Leadership and project management can support the core, but a separate plan built around them would lose the defining engineering and technology inquiry. No third distinct plan is supported.

notes.text: UCR brings together sustainable materials, product prototyping, energy design, computing and business. Maastricht builds on a dedicated sequence in engineering fundamentals, materials, industrial processes and experimental laboratory work, with projects that apply those subjects.

Maastricht requires nine 5 EC choices from its Business Engineering list and a 20 EC thesis package. The package includes preparation, an internship, and an individual paper, presentation and defence. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the displayed 180 EC schedule.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Business Engineering combines mathematics, engineering and business. Students apply those subjects in projects on market research, circular design, engineering and commercialisation before completing a thesis research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR option combines sustainable technology and business. The other concentrates on software, modelling and data in a business context. Maastricht adds a longer sequence of engineering projects and laboratory work and a required internship and thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The standard pathway includes 45 EC of choices from the Business Engineering list and a 20 EC thesis package, including 2.5 EC of preparation.

componentNotes.y3-04: Students must be in year three and complete all first-year components before starting the thesis research. The Internship Office approves participation.
